one_line_thesis: New URC is a levered Green River trona-royalty and Wyoming land estate funding a uranium royalty platform; interesting vehicle, rich security at deemed US$3.64 and still not cheap at a US$2.96 listing proxy on midcycle cash.

deep_dive.executive_summary: At a US$2.96 listing proxy (UROY last print on a 1-for-1 exchange into New URC), the base case owner path is about −12.4% per year over seven years if midcycle cash only partially recovers and land/uranium options stay half-recognized. That is not an accumulate signal on cash alone. The bull path (operator capacity growth, soda-ash cycle normalization, uranium and Wyoming land options) can still approach breakeven to low-single-digit positive returns, which is why Power Zone personas disagree on urgency. Marvin proposes watch until listing tape, debt covenants, and midcycle cash are clearer.

industry.structure: Green River trona/soda ash production is oligopolistic (WE Soda, Tata, Sisecam, Solvay/American Soda); royalty owners collect capital-free checks on half the checkerboard basin via KSLA. Uranium royalties are fragmented among small specialists (URC, GROY, EMX-style names) and larger precious-metals royalty firms.
industry.share_shift: Sweetwater consolidation into a public NASDAQ vehicle concentrates Wyoming trona royalties under New URC; synthetic soda ash supply growth has pressured natural trona pricing and royalty volumes industry-wide.
industry.trend: Soda ash at generational lows per basin operator commentary; uranium optionality re-emerges on restart and price but remains small versus trona cash in the combined company. Land monetization (data centers, renewables) is aspirational across large Wyoming fee estates.
